column1: # One row per api the port carries here: what this host's own camera answers, what the port answers, and why
# the two columns differ where they do. The host column is measured by this run; the port column is the
# answer for the devices of this port's bands (an iPhone 4S, an iPad 2), which is the reason in the note.

column4: why they differ, or what both are
the host's camera has the hardware; the port's devices have none, so the list of types that can be performed is empty
the same: YES where "resources for reactions are available on the device instance" (AVCaptureDevice.h:2471)
neither camera nor device has a reaction running; both answer 0
the host's camera reports YES for all seven of its formats (measured); the port's devices cannot
a format runs reactions only where it reports reactionEffectsSupported, and the port's do not; every format of the host's camera reports YES and a 15-30 range (measured)
both empty: this host's camera has no depth sensor either, so this row is not the port's judgement alone
both NO, measured on the host's own camera

the header's iOS rule is the application's own UIBackgroundModes or its NSCameraReactionEffectsEnabled opt-in (AVCaptureDevice.h:2448); the host's rule is macOS's, "enabled by default for all applications". The four-Info.plists phase checks both branches of the port's rule

the host reflects this Mac's Control Center Gestures setting (AVCaptureDevice.h:2458); the port answers the documented default, "gesture detection is enabled" (:2461), which an application may change from 17.4 on with NSCameraReactionEffectGesturesEnabledDefault. The four-Info.plists phase checks both branches

the port answers the release's own best camera, +defaultDeviceWithMediaType: over the two cameras of a device of its bands, which is the one on the back (tests/backports/device/avcapture.m:91 measured the back camera first in that list on an iPhone 4S; AVCaptureDevice.h:120 says the video default is "the built in camera that is primarily used for capture and recording"). The host's nil is NOT Apple's answer for this row: this process's camera authorization is notDetermined, which the PREFCAM host line prints beside it, and a process that was never granted access answers nil

both nil before an application sets one, measured on the host too. The port's own rules - a short history, "always a device that is present", nil only with no camera, and a nil set with no effect - are checked step by step in the preferred-camera phase below, not by this row

column1: # The 18.0 slice of the same family, and the phases its own questions need. Each row is the answer both sides
column2: # gave in one run, and the fourth column says where they differ and why. The host column is measured by this
column3: # run every time; the port column is the answer for the devices of this port's bands, an iPhone 4S and an
column4: # iPad 2 with a camera on each side and ONE microphone (measured on both).

both NO. The header's default: 'When you change the device's active format, this property resets to its default value of false' (AVCaptureDevice.h:399). The host's camera has no auto video frame rate either, and its setter refuses for the same reason this one does
both NO: nothing can start Background Replacement here. The host's camera has the feature but none is running

both NO, and for the same reason: 'A class property indicating whether the user has enabled the Background Replacement feature for this application' (:2521) - no user of this release has such a setting to enable, and this Mac's Control Center has it switched off

the one row whose two columns differ for a display reason the header names: the multiplier exists 'In some system user interfaces ... [that] might differ from the videoZoomFactor property value on the receiver by a fixed ratio' (:1987), and the header's own example of one is the macOS Video Effects Menu, which this Mac has and displays the zoom at half. This release has no system interface that displays a video zoom factor, so the ratio is the identity
both empty: no scene is amenable to a spatial capture that this hardware cannot make (:2673), and this Mac's single-lens camera has no spatial capture either
both NO, for all seven of the host's formats as well as for every format here: the feature lowers the frame rate under low light and neither camera has it (:3508)
the hardware: 'This property returns YES if the format supports Background Replacement' (:3736), and this Mac's camera has it for all seven formats while a single-lens camera from 2010 has not
both NO: capturing a spatial video needs the two views a depth map is computed from, and neither camera has two lenses (:3553)

both nil, the header's own answer for the case: 'When a recommendation is not available, this property returns nil' (:3309). A recommendation is a system's own exposure control's range, and AVCaptureSystemExposureBiasSlider arrived with iOS 18
both nil, by the same sentence of the same kind (:3277); the system range here would be AVCaptureSystemZoomSlider's, which is iOS 18's too

the pairing the header states (:3746): a format that supports Background Replacement has the limited range, and one that does not answers nil. The host's camera supports it, this port's devices do not

both AVCaptureMultichannelAudioModeNone, 'The default value is AVCaptureMultichannelAudioModeNone, in which case the default single channel audio recording is used' (:395) - what one microphone records
both NO, and the setter phase below is what shows that this is a value and not a refusal: Apple's own setter keeps what it was given on an input whose windNoiseRemovalSupported is 0

both NO: 'YES if the device supports wind noise removal, NO otherwise' (:405), and separating one voice from the wind around it needs several microphones. This Mac's built-in microphone is a single one as well
